title: Affinity Slice Recommender and Safe Deployment for KV Cache Economics
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: build an automated recommender that groups prefixes into affinity slices, predicts per-slice hit-rates and marginal cost savings from TTL/policy changes, and applies safe staged config changes with automatic rollback. This ticket covers modeling, simulator, config applier, and rollout gates. Key constraints: preserve latency SLOs, avoid customer-visible correctness regressions, and ensure predictable unit-cost savings. We will favor conservative changes initially and provide clear operator undo paths.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Recommender produces per-slice TTL and policy suggestions with expected cost delta and confidence bands for >90% of active prefixes.
A2: Simulation harness can replay 14 days of traffic and predict hit-rate within ±5% against held-out telemetry.
A3: Staged applier supports shadow canary + 5-step ramp with automatic reversion triggers (cost delta, hit-rate drop, error-rate increase).
A4: Integration tests and a dry-run mode are available in the console; runbook for rollback is documented.
A5: Pilot on non-critical tenant reduces per-token cost by >=6% without violating latency SLOs for 7 days.
rollout_plan: 1) Unit and integration tests on CI. 2) Run simulator on 3 months of historical traffic to generate recommendations. 3) Shadow deploy config applier for 48h and compare simulated vs observed hit-rate. 4) Canary: 2% traffic for 24h, then 5% for 72h, monitor triggers. 5) Gradual 10->30->100% rollout if no triggers. Auto-revert thresholds: cost regression >10% of expected saving OR hit-rate drop >15% absolute OR latency SLO violation. Manual unblock required after auto-revert.

decision_log: Model choice: hierarchical Bayesian hit-rate predictor + survival-analysis-derived TTL suggestion. Trade-offs: Bayesian model increases compute for training but reduces noisy false positives among low-volume prefixes. We chose to bias TTL proposals conservatively (multiply survival estimate by 0.7) to favor stability. Rollback: automated monitor will auto-revert config changes on threshold violation and create an incident ticket with diagnostic bundle.
steps: 1. Feature engineering: compute per-prefix affinity features (entropy, inter-request gap distribution, batch co-occurrence, tenant sensitivity)
2. Train Bayesian hierarchical hit-rate model and TTL survival estimator; validate on cross-folds
3. Build cost-benefit simulator with stochastic replay and token-cost model
4. Implement staged config applier: shadow canary, phased ramp, auto-revert hooks
5. Add console panels and dry-run mode; ship operator runbook
6. Run pilot on non-critical tenant for 7 days and evaluate against acceptance criteria
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-aggressive TTLs on bursty prefixes could increase cache misses and downstream cost. Mitigation: seasonality detector will mark prefixes as 'do-not-touch' and conservative multiplier applied.
Risk: Model drift as traffic changes. Mitigation: weekly re-training and drift alerts with automatic freeze of recommendations if drift > 12%.
Risk: Canary traffic might not be representative. Mitigation: choose multiple tenants with varied traffic patterns and maintain a fallback to previous policy for critical customers.
